source.text: שִׁמְע֞וּ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה פָּר֤וֹת הַבָּשָׁן֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּהַ֣ר שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן הָעֹשְׁק֣וֹת דַּלִּ֔ים הָרֹצְצ֖וֹת אֶבְיוֹנִ֑ים הָאֹמְרֹ֥ת לַאֲדֹֽנֵיהֶ֖ם הָבִ֥יאָה וְנִשְׁתֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Hear this word, cows of the Bashan who [are] on [the] mountain of Samaria, who oppress [the] poor, who crush [the] needy, who say to their lords: Bring, and let us drink.

en.L: Hear this word, cows of Bashan, you who [are] on the mount of Samaria, \q you who oppress the poor, \q who crush the needy, \q who say to their lords, "Bring, and let us drink!"
en.B: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on the hill of Samaria, \q you who oppress the poor \q and crush the needy, \q who say to their husbands, "Bring us something to drink!"
en.R: Listen to this message, you women of Samaria, as fat as the cows of Bashan. \q You mistreat poor people \q and crush those in need. \q You say to your husbands, "Bring us more to drink!"

es.L: {{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}} esta palabra, vacas de Basán, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}} que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} en el monte de Samaria, \q que {{plural_you:oprimen|oprimís}} a los pobres, \q que {{plural_you:aplastan|aplastáis}} a los necesitados, \q que {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} a sus señores: «¡Trae, y bebamos!».
es.B: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} esta palabra, vacas de Basán que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} en el monte de Samaria, \q {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}} que {{plural_you:oprimen|oprimís}} a los pobres \q y {{plural_you:aplastan|aplastáis}} a los necesitados, \q que {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} a sus maridos: «¡Tráenos algo de beber!».
es.R: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} este mensaje, mujeres de Samaria, gordas como las vacas de Basán. \q {{plural_you:Maltratan|Maltratáis}} a los pobres \q y {{plural_you:aplastan|aplastáis}} a los necesitados. \q Les {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} a {{plural_you:sus maridos|vuestros maridos}}: «¡Tráenos más de beber!».

fr.L: Écoutez cette parole, vaches du Bashân, vous qui [êtes] sur la montagne de Samarie, \q vous qui opprimez les pauvres, \q qui écrasez les indigents, \q qui dites à leurs maîtres : « Apporte, et buvons ! »
fr.B: Écoutez cette parole, vaches du Bashân, sur la colline de Samarie, \q vous qui opprimez les pauvres \q et écrasez les indigents, \q qui dites à vos maris : « Apportez-nous à boire ! »
fr.R: Écoutez ce message, femmes de Samarie, grasses comme les vaches du Bashân. \q Vous maltraitez les pauvres \q et vous écrasez ceux qui sont dans le besoin. \q Vous dites à vos maris : « Apportez-nous encore à boire ! »

sw.L: Sikieni neno hili, enyi ng'ombe wa Bashani, mlio juu ya mlima wa Samaria, \q ninyi mnaowaonea maskini, \q mnaowaponda wahitaji, \q mnaowaambia mabwana zenu, "Leteni, tunywe!"
sw.B: Sikilizeni neno hili, enyi ng'ombe wa Bashani mlio juu ya kilima cha Samaria, \q ninyi mnaowaonea maskini \q na kuwaponda wahitaji, \q mnaowaambia waume zenu, "Tuleteeni kitu cha kunywa!"
sw.R: Sikilizeni ujumbe huu, enyi wanawake wa Samaria mlionona kama ng'ombe wa Bashani. \q Mnawatendea maskini mabaya \q na kuwaponda wahitaji. \q Mnawaambia waume zenu, "Tuleteeni vinywaji zaidi!"

vi.L: Hãy nghe lời này, hỡi những con bò cái của Ba-san, các ngươi là những kẻ ở trên núi Sa-ma-ri, \q các ngươi là những kẻ áp bức người nghèo, \q chà đạp người túng thiếu, \q và nói với các chủ của mình: "Hãy đem đến, cho chúng ta uống!"
vi.B: Hãy nghe lời này, hỡi những con bò cái Ba-san trên đồi Sa-ma-ri, \q các ngươi là những kẻ áp bức người nghèo \q và chà đạp người túng thiếu, \q là những kẻ nói với chồng mình: "Đem rượu đến cho chúng tôi uống!"
vi.R: Hãy nghe sứ điệp này, hỡi các bà ở Sa-ma-ri, béo tốt như những con bò cái Ba-san. \q Các ngươi ngược đãi người nghèo \q và chà đạp những người túng thiếu. \q Các ngươi bảo chồng mình: "Đem thêm rượu đến cho chúng tôi uống!"

ko.L: 사마리아 산에 있는 바산의 암소들아, 이 말을 들어라. \q 가난한 자들을 억압하고, \q 궁핍한 자들을 짓밟으며, \q 자기 주인들에게 "가져오너라, 우리가 마시자!" 하고 말하는 자들아.
ko.B: 사마리아 언덕에 사는 바산의 암소들아, 이 말을 들어라. \q 너희는 가난한 사람들을 억압하고 \q 궁핍한 사람들을 짓밟으며, \q 남편들에게 "마실 것을 가져와요!" 하고 말한다.
ko.R: 바산의 암소들처럼 살진 사마리아의 여자들아, 이 말을 들어라. \q 너희는 가난한 사람들을 괴롭히고 \q 어려운 사람들을 짓밟는다. \q 너희는 남편들에게 "술을 더 가져와요!" 하고 말한다.

decisions.choice: cows of Bashan: the sleek, well-fed cattle of the richest grazing land
decisions.reason: Bashan was the high plateau east of the Sea of Galilee, famous for its rich pasture and its strong, well-fed cattle (Deuteronomy 32:14; Psalm 22:13; Ezekiel 39:18). To call people "cows of Bashan" pictures them as pampered and fat on the best of everything, while they live off the poor. Verses 2-3 show where such cattle end up: led away through the breaches.

decisions.choice: the cows are the wealthy women of Samaria
alternatives: the rich rulers of Samaria, men and women
decisions.reason: The participles "who oppress", "who crush" and "who say" are feminine, and in verse 3 "each woman" goes out through the breaches. They speak to "their lords", their husbands. So the words are addressed to the rich women of the capital. Some pronouns in verses 1-3 are masculine ("their lords", "upon you" in verse 2), a mixing found elsewhere in Hebrew, and some take the "cows" more widely, as the rich and powerful of Samaria, men and women alike.

decisions.choice: their lords: their husbands
decisions.reason: A wife could call her husband "my lord" (Genesis 18:12; Judges 19:26-27). The word also hints at the irony: the women give the orders, and their "lords" obey.

decisions.choice: oppress the poor ... "Bring, and let us drink!": their drinking is paid for by the poor
decisions.reason: The women may not oppress the poor with their own hands, but their demands for wine drive their husbands to squeeze the poor for it. The same pair, "the poor" and "the needy", stands in 2:6-7 and 8:4-6.

decisions.choice: you women of Samaria, as fat as the cows of Bashan (R); husbands (B, R); lords (L)
decisions.reason: Readable says who the "cows" are and what the picture means, following m2. Since m2 is uncertain, so is this wording. Balanced and Readable say "husbands" for "lords" (m3); Readable says "your husbands" because it speaks to the women directly throughout.

decisions.choice: plural_you in the feminine ("ustedes" / "vosotras") for the women of Samaria
decisions.reason: The rich women are addressed as a group, so every "you" in 4:1-3 is a plural_you span whose vosotros option is feminine ("vosotras", "arrastradas"), as 1 Peter 3:1-5 in Spanish. The Hebrew "their lords" switches to the third person; L and B keep it ("sus señores", "sus maridos"), R says "your" as the English does.

decisions.choice: "sus señores" (L); "sus maridos" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Adon of a husband is kept word for word at L; B and R say who is meant.

decisions.choice: "vaches du Bashân" with feminine "vous" (L, B); "femmes de Samarie, grasses comme les vaches du Bashân" (R); "leurs maîtres" (L), "vos maris" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The rich women of Samaria are addressed as a group, in the second person plural, and Literal keeps the Hebrew's switch to "their lords"; Bashan keeps the form of the published French ("le Bashân"). The cry "Bring" is singular in Hebrew, said to each husband, so Literal has "Apporte".

decisions.choice: "mabwana zenu" (L); "waume zenu" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "their lords"; the Swahili uses "zenu" (your) because the women are addressed directly, which Swahili prefers to a switch from "you" to "their" within the sentence.

decisions.choice: "những con bò cái của Ba-san" (L, B); "các bà ở Sa-ma-ri, béo tốt như những con bò cái Ba-san" (R)
decisions.reason: The cows are the rich women of Samaria (meaning decision); Literal and Balanced keep Amos's picture with "bò cái", and Readable names the women, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: The women's words to their husbands are 해요체 ("가져와요") at B and R; L keeps the Hebrew "주인들" with plain 해라체
decisions.reason: The term sheet gives 해요체 for husband and wife (Genesis note, Hosea 3); the demand is a wife's to her husband, while Literal keeps the Hebrew "lords".

decisions.choice: "các chủ của mình" (L); "chồng mình" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Their "lords" are their husbands (meaning decision); Literal keeps "chủ", lowercase, and the others say "chồng".

source.text: נִשְׁבַּ֨ע אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ בְּקָדְשׁ֔וֹ כִּ֛י הִנֵּ֥ה יָמִ֖ים בָּאִ֣ים עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְנִשָּׂ֤א אֶתְכֶם֙ בְּצִנּ֔וֹת וְאַחֲרִיתְכֶ֖ן בְּסִיר֥וֹת דּוּגָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Has sworn [the] Lord Yahweh by his holiness: For look, days [are] coming upon you, and one will lift you away with hooks, and your remnant with fishhooks.

en.L: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has sworn by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holiness: \q Look, days are coming upon you \q when they will carry you away with hooks, \q and the last of you with fishhooks.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has sworn by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holiness: \q The time is surely coming for you \q when you will be dragged away with hooks, \q the last of you with fishhooks.
en.R: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has made a solemn promise by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own holiness: \q The time is coming for you \q when your enemies will drag you away with hooks, \q every last one of you, like fish on hooks.

es.L: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} ha jurado por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santidad: \q He aquí, vienen días sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}} \q en que {{plural_you:las|os}} llevarán con garfios, \q y a {{plural_you:las últimas de ustedes|vuestras últimas}} con anzuelos de pesca.
es.B: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} ha jurado por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} santidad: \q Ciertamente viene el tiempo para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}} \q en que {{plural_you:serán arrastradas|seréis arrastradas}} con garfios, \q y hasta la última con anzuelos.
es.R: El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} ha hecho un juramento solemne por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia santidad: \q Viene el tiempo para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}} \q en que {{plural_you:sus enemigos las|vuestros enemigos os}} arrastrarán con garfios, \q hasta la última, como peces en el anzuelo.

fr.L: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} l’a juré par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sainteté : \q Voici, des jours viennent sur vous \q où l’on vous enlèvera avec des crocs, \q et les dernières d’entre vous avec des hameçons.
fr.B: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} l’a juré par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} sainteté : \q Le temps vient pour vous, c’est certain, \q où vous serez traînées au loin avec des crocs, \q et les dernières d’entre vous avec des hameçons.
fr.R: Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} l’a promis solennellement par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} propre sainteté : \q Le temps vient pour vous \q où vos ennemis vous traîneront au loin avec des crocs, \q toutes, jusqu’à la dernière, comme des poissons au bout d’un hameçon.

sw.L: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} ameapa kwa utakatifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}: \q Tazama, siku zinawajia \q watakapowachukua kwa kulabu, \q na wale wa mwisho wenu kwa ndoana.
sw.B: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} ameapa kwa utakatifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}: \q Hakika wakati unawajia \q mtakapoburutwa kwa kulabu, \q wa mwisho wenu kwa ndoana.
sw.R: Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} ameahidi kwa kiapo kwa utakatifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}: \q Wakati unawajia \q adui zenu watakapowaburuta kwa kulabu, \q kila mmoja wenu hadi wa mwisho, kama samaki kwenye ndoana.

vi.L: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã chỉ sự thánh khiết của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà thề: \q Này, những ngày sắp đến trên các ngươi, \q khi người ta sẽ dùng móc mà kéo các ngươi đi, \q và những kẻ sót lại của các ngươi bằng lưỡi câu.
vi.B: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã chỉ sự thánh khiết của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà thề: \q Chắc chắn thời kỳ đang đến cho các ngươi, \q khi các ngươi sẽ bị kéo đi bằng móc sắt, \q người cuối cùng của các ngươi bằng lưỡi câu.
vi.R: Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã lấy chính sự thánh khiết của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà hứa long trọng: \q Thời kỳ đang đến cho các ngươi, \q khi kẻ thù sẽ dùng móc kéo các ngươi đi, \q đến người cuối cùng, như cá mắc lưỡi câu.

ko.L: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 그분의 거룩하심을 두고 맹세하셨다. \q 보라, 날들이 너희에게 오고 있다. \q 그때에 그들이 너희를 갈고리로 끌어가고, \q 너희 가운데 남은 자들을 낚싯바늘로 [끌어갈 것이다].
ko.B: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 그분의 거룩하심을 두고 맹세하셨다. \q 너희에게 반드시 그때가 온다. \q 너희가 갈고리에 꿰여 끌려가고, \q 너희 가운데 마지막 사람까지 낚싯바늘에 꿰여 끌려갈 것이다.
ko.R: 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 그분의 거룩하심을 걸고 엄숙하게 약속하셨다. \q 너희에게 그때가 오고 있다. \q 그때에 원수들이 너희를 갈고리로 끌고 갈 것이다. \q 너희는 한 사람도 남김없이 낚싯바늘에 걸린 물고기처럼 끌려갈 것이다.

decisions.choice: sworn by his holiness: the LORD swears by what he is, so the oath cannot fail
decisions.reason: People swear by something greater than themselves; the LORD can swear only by himself (6:8), by his holiness (Psalm 89:36), or by what he has made his own (8:7). His holiness stands against the profaning of his name (2:7). It is the surest of oaths.

decisions.choice: days are coming: the time is coming
decisions.reason: The phrase announces a coming time of judgment or of restoration (8:11; 9:13; Jeremiah 7:32).

decisions.choice: hooks ... fishhooks: the captives are dragged away like fish on hooks
alternatives: carried away in baskets, the last of you in fish pots
decisions.reason: Both words are rare. They are usually taken as hooks or barbs, the second as fishing hooks, and conquerors are pictured leading captives with hooks (2 Kings 19:28; Ezekiel 19:4; 29:4). The words can also mean thorns and pots, so that the people are carried off in baskets as fish were. "The last of you" may also be "your descendants". On every reading, the cows of Bashan are taken away like animals or fish.

decisions.choice: they will carry you away: the enemy, not named
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject ("one will lift you away"), as Hebrew does when the doer does not matter. It is the enemy of 3:11.

decisions.choice: The time is surely coming (B); has made a solemn promise; your enemies; like fish on hooks (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "days are coming" (m2). Readable explains the oath and names the enemy as the doer (m4).

decisions.choice: "주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 그분의 거룩하심을 두고 맹세하셨다"
decisions.reason: Amos reports the oath, so God takes -시- and 그분; the oath itself is God's own words in 해라체.

source.text: וּפְרָצִ֥ים תֵּצֶ֖אנָה אִשָּׁ֣ה נֶגְדָּ֑הּ וְהִשְׁלַכְתֶּ֥נָה הַהַרְמ֖וֹנָה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And through breaches you will go out, each woman before her, and you will be cast toward the Harmon, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And through the breaches you will go out, each [woman] straight ahead, \q and you will be cast out toward Harmon, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: You will go out through the breaches in the wall, each one straight ahead, \q and you will be thrown out toward Harmon, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: You will go out through the holes in the broken walls, each of you straight ahead, \q and you will be thrown out toward Harmon, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y por las brechas {{plural_you:saldrán|saldréis}}, cada [una] derecho delante de sí, \q y {{plural_you:serán arrojadas|seréis arrojadas}} hacia Harmón, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Saldrán|Saldréis}} por las brechas de la muralla, cada una derecho delante de sí, \q y {{plural_you:serán arrojadas|seréis arrojadas}} hacia Harmón, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Saldrán|Saldréis}} por los huecos de las murallas derribadas, una detrás de otra, \q y {{plural_you:serán arrojadas|seréis arrojadas}} hacia Harmón, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et par les brèches vous sortirez, chacune droit devant elle, \q et vous serez jetées vers Harmôn, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Vous sortirez par les brèches de la muraille, chacune droit devant elle, \q et vous serez jetées vers Harmôn, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Vous sortirez par les trous des murailles écroulées, chacune droit devant elle, \q et vous serez jetées dehors, vers Harmôn, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nanyi mtatoka kupitia mahali palipobomoka, kila [mwanamke] moja kwa moja mbele yake, \q nanyi mtatupwa kuelekea Harmoni, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Mtatoka kupitia mahali palipobomoka ukutani, kila mmoja moja kwa moja mbele yake, \q nanyi mtatupwa nje kuelekea Harmoni, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Mtatoka kupitia mapengo ya kuta zilizobomoka, kila mmoja wenu moja kwa moja mbele yake, \q nanyi mtatupwa nje kuelekea Harmoni, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Và qua những chỗ tường thủng các ngươi sẽ đi ra, mỗi [người đàn bà] đi thẳng trước mặt mình, \q và các ngươi sẽ bị ném về phía Hạt-môn, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Các ngươi sẽ đi ra qua những lỗ thủng trên tường thành, người nào cũng đi thẳng phía trước, \q và các ngươi sẽ bị ném ra về phía Hạt-môn, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Các ngươi sẽ đi ra qua những lỗ hổng nơi tường thành đổ nát, ai nấy đi thẳng phía trước, \q và các ngươi sẽ bị ném ra về phía Hạt-môn, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 너희는 무너진 틈으로 나가되, 각자 [자기] 앞으로 [나갈 것이다]. \q 그리고 너희는 하르몬 쪽으로 내던져질 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 너희는 성벽의 무너진 틈으로 한 사람씩 곧장 끌려 나가, \q 하르몬 쪽으로 내던져질 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 너희는 무너진 성벽의 구멍으로 한 사람씩 끌려 나갈 것이다. \q 그리고 하르몬 쪽으로 내던져질 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: through the breaches ... each straight ahead: led out through the gaps in the broken walls, one behind another
decisions.reason: When a city fell, its walls were breached and its people led out through the gaps. "Each straight ahead" pictures them going in file, unable to turn aside, like cattle driven through a broken fence (compare Joshua 6:5, 20).

decisions.choice: you will be cast out: reading the verb as passive
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels give an active verb, "you will cast out", with no object, which is hard to make sense of. The same letters read with other vowels give "you will be cast out", and several ancient translations take it that way. That reading is followed here.

decisions.choice: Harmon: a place not otherwise known
decisions.reason: Harmon is named nowhere else, and its location is unknown. Some take it as Mount Hermon in the far north, on the road to exile, or read it with the ancient translations as another name; it may also be a word for a place of refuse. It is clearly the place where the captives are thrown.

decisions.choice: in the wall (B), in the broken walls (R); each one (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the breaches are (m1). Literal brackets "woman", which the Hebrew gives in a feminine word for "each".

decisions.choice: "Hạt-môn"
decisions.reason: The place is unknown (meaning decision); the name is transliterated after the Protestant pattern for Hebrew names; a reviewer may prefer another spelling.

decisions.choice: "하르몬"
decisions.reason: A place named only here (meaning decision); the name is transcribed from the Hebrew.

source.text: בֹּ֤אוּ בֵֽית־אֵל֙ וּפִשְׁע֔וּ הַגִּלְגָּ֖ל הַרְבּ֣וּ לִפְשֹׁ֑עַ וְהָבִ֤יאוּ לַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ זִבְחֵיכֶ֔ם לִשְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים מַעְשְׂרֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Come to Bethel and transgress; to the Gilgal, multiply to transgress; and bring to the morning your sacrifices, to three days your tithes.

en.L: Come to Bethel and transgress; \q to Gilgal, and multiply transgressing; \q and bring your sacrifices every morning, \q your tithes every three days;
en.B: Go to Bethel and rebel! \q Go to Gilgal and rebel even more! \q Bring your sacrifices every morning, \q your tithes every three days!
en.R: Go ahead! Go to Bethel and sin! \q Go to Gilgal and sin even more! \q Bring your sacrifices every morning \q and your tithes every three days!

es.L: {{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} a Betel y {{plural_you:transgredan|transgredid}}; \q a Gilgal, y {{plural_you:multipliquen|multiplicad}} la transgresión; \q y {{plural_you:traigan|traed}} {{plural_you:sus sacrificios|vuestros sacrificios}} cada mañana, \q {{plural_you:sus diezmos|vuestros diezmos}} cada tres días;
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a Betel y {{plural_you:rebélense|rebelaos}}! \q ¡{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a Gilgal y {{plural_you:rebélense|rebelaos}} todavía más! \q ¡{{plural_you:Traigan|Traed}} {{plural_you:sus sacrificios|vuestros sacrificios}} cada mañana, \q {{plural_you:sus diezmos|vuestros diezmos}} cada tres días!
es.R: ¡Adelante! ¡{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a Betel y {{plural_you:pequen|pecad}}! \q ¡{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a Gilgal y {{plural_you:pequen|pecad}} todavía más! \q ¡{{plural_you:Traigan|Traed}} {{plural_you:sus sacrificios|vuestros sacrificios}} cada mañana \q y {{plural_you:sus diezmos|vuestros diezmos}} cada tres días!

fr.L: Venez à Béthel, et transgressez ; \q à Guilgal, multipliez les transgressions ; \q et apportez vos sacrifices chaque matin, \q vos dîmes tous les trois jours ;
fr.B: Allez à Béthel, et révoltez-vous ! \q Allez à Guilgal, et révoltez-vous encore plus ! \q Apportez vos sacrifices chaque matin, \q vos dîmes tous les trois jours !
fr.R: Allez-y ! Allez à Béthel et péchez ! \q Allez à Guilgal et péchez encore plus ! \q Apportez vos sacrifices chaque matin \q et vos dîmes tous les trois jours !

sw.L: Njooni Betheli mkaasi; \q [njooni] Gilgali, mkaongeze kuasi; \q mkalete dhabihu zenu kila asubuhi, \q zaka zenu kila siku tatu;
sw.B: Nendeni Betheli mkaasi! \q Nendeni Gilgali mkaasi zaidi! \q Leteni dhabihu zenu kila asubuhi, \q zaka zenu kila siku tatu!
sw.R: Haya! Nendeni Betheli mkatende dhambi! \q Nendeni Gilgali mkatende dhambi zaidi! \q Leteni dhabihu zenu kila asubuhi, \q na zaka zenu kila siku tatu!

vi.L: Hãy đến Bê-tên mà vi phạm; \q [đến] Ghinh-ganh mà vi phạm thêm nhiều; \q và hãy đem sinh tế các ngươi đến mỗi buổi sáng, \q phần mười các ngươi mỗi ba ngày;
vi.B: Hãy đến Bê-tên mà phản nghịch! \q Hãy đến Ghinh-ganh mà phản nghịch thêm nữa! \q Hãy dâng sinh tế mỗi buổi sáng, \q và phần mười mỗi ba ngày!
vi.R: Cứ đi đi! Hãy đến Bê-tên mà phạm tội! \q Hãy đến Ghinh-ganh mà phạm tội thêm nữa! \q Hãy dâng sinh tế mỗi buổi sáng \q và dâng phần mười mỗi ba ngày!

ko.L: 벧엘로 가서 반역하여라. \q 길갈로 가서 반역을 더하여라. \q 아침마다 너희 제물을 가져오고, \q 사흘마다 너희 십일조를 [가져오너라].
ko.B: 벧엘로 가서 반역하여라! \q 길갈로 가서 더 반역하여라! \q 아침마다 제물을 가져오고, \q 사흘마다 십일조를 바쳐라!
ko.R: 어디 해 보아라! 벧엘로 가서 죄를 지어라! \q 길갈로 가서 죄를 더 지어라! \q 아침마다 제물을 가져오고, \q 사흘마다 십일조를 바쳐라!

decisions.choice: Come to Bethel and transgress: a priest's call to worship, turned upside down
decisions.reason: A priest would call pilgrims to "come" to the shrine and worship. Amos uses the same words to say "come and transgress": their worship itself is rebellion against the LORD, because they offer it while oppressing the poor (5:4-5, 21-24).

decisions.choice: Bethel and Gilgal: the main shrines of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Bethel was the royal shrine (3:14; 7:13). Gilgal, near Jericho, was where Israel first camped in the land and where Saul was made king (Joshua 4:19-20; 1 Samuel 11:15). Both were busy places of pilgrimage, condemned also by Hosea (Hosea 4:15; 9:15) and in Amos 5:5.

decisions.choice: every morning ... every three days: worship carried far beyond what the law asked
alternatives: on the morning (after you arrive) ... on the third day
decisions.reason: Tithes were brought once a year, and every third year for the poor (Deuteronomy 14:22-29), and sacrifices at the feasts. Bringing sacrifices daily and tithes every three days is sarcasm: the more zealous their worship, the more they sin. Some read the phrases as "in the morning" and "on the third day" of a pilgrimage, the days on which offerings were brought after arrival.

decisions.choice: transgress (L), rebel (B), sin (R)
decisions.reason: The verb belongs with the noun "transgression" of the refrain of chapters 1-2. It follows Amos's settled wording for the noun: "transgression" (Literal), "crime / rebellion" (Balanced) and "sin" (Readable). Balanced says "rebel" because here the wrong is done against God. Balanced and Readable repeat "Go" in the second line, which the Hebrew leaves implied; Readable adds "Go ahead!" to mark the sarcasm.

decisions.choice: "transgredir" (L), "rebelarse" (B), "pecar" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb pasha' as the terms note sets for these books.

decisions.choice: "transgressez" (L), "révoltez-vous" (B), "péchez" (R) for the verb pasha
decisions.reason: The verb follows the noun's wording in the Twelve: transgress, rebel, sin. Balanced "se révolter" keeps the rebellion against an authority that the word means.

decisions.choice: "kuasi" (L, B); "kutenda dhambi" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb pasha', as the term sheet sets for these books.

decisions.choice: "vi phạm" (L); "phản nghịch" (B); "phạm tội" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb pasha' takes the terms-sheet words: transgress / rebel / sin.

decisions.choice: The verb *pasha'* is "반역하다" (L, B) and "죄를 짓다" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording; the summons to worship is turned into a summons to rebel, so the ironic imperatives stay.

source.text: וְקַטֵּ֤ר מֵֽחָמֵץ֙ תּוֹדָ֔ה וְקִרְא֥וּ נְדָב֖וֹת הַשְׁמִ֑יעוּ כִּ֣י כֵ֤ן אֲהַבְתֶּם֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And burn from leavened [bread] a thank offering, and proclaim freewill offerings, make [them] heard; for so you love, sons of Israel, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: and burn a thank offering of leavened bread, \q and proclaim freewill offerings, make [them] heard; \q for so you love [to do], {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Burn a thank offering of leavened bread, \q and announce your freewill offerings, make them known! \q For this is what you love to do, {{gender:people|sons}} of Israel, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Burn bread made with yeast as a thank offering. \q Tell everyone about the gifts you bring freely, and make sure they hear! \q People of Israel, this is the kind of thing you love to do, \q says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: y {{plural_you:quemen|quemad}} pan con levadura como ofrenda de acción de gracias, \q y {{plural_you:proclamen|proclamad}} ofrendas voluntarias, {{plural_you:háganlas|hacedlas}} oír; \q porque así lo {{plural_you:aman|amáis}}, hijos de Israel, \q declara el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Quemen|Quemad}} pan con levadura como ofrenda de acción de gracias, \q y {{plural_you:anuncien|anunciad}} {{plural_you:sus ofrendas voluntarias|vuestras ofrendas voluntarias}}, {{plural_you:dénlas|dadlas}} a conocer! \q Porque esto es lo que {{plural_you:a ustedes les encanta|a vosotros os encanta}} hacer, israelitas, \q afirma el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Quemen|Quemad}} pan hecho con levadura como ofrenda de acción de gracias. \q ¡{{plural_you:Cuéntenles|Contad}} a todos las ofrendas que {{plural_you:traen|traéis}} voluntariamente, y {{plural_you:asegúrense|aseguraos}} de que lo oigan! \q Pueblo de Israel, esto es lo que {{plural_you:a ustedes les encanta|a vosotros os encanta}} hacer, \q dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: et faites fumer du pain levé en offrande de reconnaissance, \q et proclamez les offrandes volontaires, faites[-les] entendre ; \q car c’est ainsi que vous aimez [faire], {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, \q déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Faites brûler du pain levé en offrande de reconnaissance, \q et annoncez vos offrandes volontaires, faites-les savoir ! \q Car c’est ce que vous aimez faire, {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, \q déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Brûlez du pain fait avec du levain en offrande de reconnaissance. \q Parlez à tout le monde des dons que vous apportez librement, et veillez à ce qu’on les entende ! \q {{gender:Israélites|Fils d’Israël}}, voilà le genre de choses que vous aimez faire, \q dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: na kuteketeza sadaka ya shukrani ya [mkate] uliotiwa chachu, \q na kutangaza sadaka za hiari, kuzitangaza [ili zisikike]; \q kwa maana ndivyo mpendavyo [kufanya], enyi wana wa Israeli, \q asema Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Teketezeni sadaka ya shukrani ya mkate uliotiwa chachu, \q na kutangaza sadaka zenu za hiari, zijulikane! \q Kwa maana hivi ndivyo mnavyopenda kufanya, enyi wana wa Israeli, \q asema Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Teketezeni mkate uliotiwa chachu kama sadaka ya shukrani. \q Mwambieni kila mtu habari za zawadi mnazotoa kwa hiari, mhakikishe wanasikia! \q Enyi watu wa Israeli, mambo ya namna hii ndiyo mnayopenda kufanya, \q anasema Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: và hãy đốt tế lễ tạ ơn bằng bánh có men, \q và hãy rao báo các tế lễ tự nguyện, cho [người ta] nghe; \q vì các ngươi thích [làm] như vậy, hỡi con cái Y-sơ-ra-ên, \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Hãy đốt bánh có men làm tế lễ tạ ơn, \q hãy rao báo các tế lễ tự nguyện của các ngươi, cho mọi người biết! \q Vì đó là điều các ngươi thích làm, hỡi dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Hãy đốt bánh làm bằng men làm tế lễ tạ ơn. \q Hãy khoe với mọi người về những lễ vật các ngươi tự nguyện dâng, và lo sao cho họ nghe thấy! \q Hỡi dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, đó là loại việc các ngươi thích làm, \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 누룩 넣은 [빵으로] 감사 제물을 불사르고, \q 자원 제물을 선포하여 [사람들이] 듣게 하여라. \q {{gender:이스라엘 자손|이스라엘의 아들들}}아, 너희가 이렇게 [하기를] 좋아하지 않느냐? \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 누룩 넣은 빵을 감사 제물로 불사르고, \q 자원 제물을 바친다고 떠들썩하게 알려라! \q {{gender:이스라엘 백성|이스라엘의 아들들}}아, 너희가 좋아하는 것이 바로 이런 것이 아니냐? \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}의 말이다.
ko.R: 누룩을 넣은 빵을 감사 제물로 태워라. \q 스스로 바치는 예물을 모든 사람에게 자랑하여라! \q 이스라엘 백성아, 너희가 좋아하는 것이 바로 이런 일이다. \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}의 말이다.

decisions.choice: burn a thank offering of leavened bread: an offering made in a way the law did not allow
decisions.reason: Nothing with leaven (yeast) was to be burned on the altar (Leviticus 2:11). With a thank offering, loaves of leavened bread were brought to be eaten, not burned (Leviticus 7:13). Burning it may show that their worship pleases themselves rather than keeping to what the LORD asked.

decisions.choice: proclaim freewill offerings, make them heard: showing off gifts that should be given freely
decisions.reason: A freewill offering was a gift beyond what was required (Leviticus 7:16; 22:18). They announce theirs publicly, so that everyone knows how generous they are.

decisions.choice: for so you love: this is the religion you enjoy
decisions.reason: The point of the sarcasm: they love their worship, but it is worship that suits them, not the LORD (5:21-23).

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B), says the Lord GOD (R); children (sons) of Israel (L), people (sons) of Israel (B), People of Israel (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this formula follows Ezekiel's table: "declares the Lord GOD" at Literal and Balanced and "says the Lord GOD" at Readable. Literal begins with "and", since the Hebrew sentence runs on from verse 4.

decisions.choice: "ofrenda de acción de gracias"; "ofrendas voluntarias"
decisions.reason: The offerings in the words of the Spanish of Leviticus 7:12 and 22:18, 29.

decisions.choice: "con cái Y-sơ-ra-ên" (L), "dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "sons" as a gender setting; Vietnamese "con cái" and "dân" already cover both, as at 1:13, so no span is needed.

source.text: וְגַם־אֲנִי֩ נָתַ֨תִּי לָכֶ֜ם נִקְי֤וֹן שִׁנַּ֨יִם֙ בְּכָל־עָ֣רֵיכֶ֔ם וְחֹ֣סֶר לֶ֔חֶם בְּכֹ֖ל מְקוֹמֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And also I gave to you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your places; yet not you returned to me, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And I also gave you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, \q and shortage of bread \q in all your places; \q yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I also gave you clean teeth in all your cities \q and lack of bread in all your towns. \q Yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I made you go hungry in all your cities. \q There was no food anywhere you lived. \q But even then you did not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y también yo {{plural_you:les|os}} di limpieza de dientes en todas {{plural_you:sus ciudades|vuestras ciudades}}, \q y falta de pan \q en todos {{plural_you:sus lugares|vuestros lugares}}; \q y no {{plural_you:volvieron|volvisteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: También {{plural_you:les|os}} di dientes limpios en todas {{plural_you:sus ciudades|vuestras ciudades}} \q y falta de pan en todos {{plural_you:sus pueblos|vuestros pueblos}}. \q Pero no {{plural_you:volvieron|volvisteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Hice que {{plural_you:pasaran|pasarais}} hambre en todas {{plural_you:sus ciudades|vuestras ciudades}}. \q No había comida en ningún lugar donde {{plural_you:vivían|vivíais}}. \q Pero aun así no {{plural_you:regresaron|regresasteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi, je vous ai donné la propreté des dents dans toutes vos villes, \q et le manque de pain \q dans tous vos lieux ; \q et vous n’êtes pas revenus à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Moi aussi, je vous ai donné des dents propres dans toutes vos villes \q et le manque de pain dans toutes vos localités. \q Pourtant, vous n’êtes pas revenus à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Je vous ai fait souffrir de la faim dans toutes vos villes. \q Il n’y avait de nourriture nulle part où vous viviez. \q Mais même alors, vous n’êtes pas revenus vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nami pia niliwapa usafi wa meno katika miji yenu yote, \q na upungufu wa mkate \q mahali penu pote; \q lakini hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Pia niliwapa meno safi katika miji yenu yote \q na ukosefu wa mkate katika vijiji vyenu vyote. \q Hata hivyo hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Niliwafanya muone njaa katika miji yenu yote. \q Hakukuwa na chakula popote mlipoishi. \q Lakini hata hivyo hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng đã cho các ngươi răng sạch trơn trong mọi thành của các ngươi, \q và sự thiếu bánh \q trong mọi nơi các ngươi ở; \q thế mà các ngươi vẫn không quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Ta cũng đã cho răng các ngươi sạch trơn trong mọi thành \q và để các ngươi thiếu bánh trong mọi thị trấn. \q Thế mà các ngươi vẫn không quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Ta đã làm cho các ngươi đói khát trong mọi thành. \q Không còn thức ăn ở bất cứ nơi nào các ngươi sống. \q Dù vậy, các ngươi vẫn không ăn năn quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 너희의 모든 성읍에서 너희에게 이를 깨끗하게 하고, \q 너희의 모든 곳에서 \q 빵이 떨어지게 했다. \q 그러나 너희는 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 내가 너희의 모든 성읍에서 너희의 이를 깨끗하게 하고 \q 너희의 모든 마을에서 빵이 떨어지게 했다. \q 그래도 너희는 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 나는 너희가 사는 모든 성읍에서 너희를 굶주리게 했다. \q 너희가 사는 곳 어디에도 먹을 것이 없었다. \q 그래도 너희는 여전히 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: cleanness of teeth: nothing to chew, famine
decisions.reason: Teeth stay clean when there is nothing to eat. The parallel line says it plainly: lack of bread.

decisions.choice: yet you did not return to me: you did not turn back to the LORD; the refrain of verses 6-11
decisions.reason: To "return" to the LORD is to come back to him in repentance and loyalty (Deuteronomy 4:30; Hosea 6:1; 14:2). The Hebrew says "return as far as me", the same words as Hosea 14:2 and Joel 2:12: a coming back all the way to the LORD himself, not a gesture toward him. Each blow in verses 6-11 was meant to bring Israel back, and each ends with the same words. The wording is kept the same in all five, and the notes here apply to all of them.

decisions.choice: famine, drought, blight, locusts, plague, sword and overthrow: the warnings of the covenant
decisions.reason: The blows of verses 6-11 match the curses the covenant warned of if Israel turned away (Leviticus 26:14-39; Deuteronomy 28:15-68), and the disasters Solomon asked the LORD to hear Israel's prayers in (1 Kings 8:33-40). In Leviticus 26 the warnings come in rounds, each one asking whether Israel will now listen. The LORD "gave" famine as they "brought" their sacrifices (verse 4).

decisions.choice: the refrain: yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD (L); Yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD (B); But even then you did not come back to me, says the LORD (R)
decisions.reason: This wording is used unchanged in verses 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11. Literal and Balanced keep the key word "return", which is also the word for repenting. Readable says "come back" and adds "even then" to show that the people did not turn back even after each blow. The closing formula follows the settled "declares the LORD" / "says the LORD".

decisions.choice: clean teeth (B); go hungry, no food (R); towns (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of clean teeth, which the parallel line explains; Readable says what it means (m1). "Places" means the places where people lived: their towns.

decisions.choice: "y no volvieron a mí, declara el SEÑOR" (L); "Pero no volvieron a mí, afirma el SEÑOR" (B); "Pero aun así no regresaron a mí, dice el SEÑOR" (R)
decisions.reason: The refrain of 4:6-11 keeps one wording at each level, with plural_you; shuv is "volver", never "arrepentirse", as the Spanish terms note for Jeremiah sets.

decisions.choice: the refrain of 4:6-11: "et vous n'êtes pas revenus à moi, déclare le SEIGNEUR" (L); "Pourtant, vous n'êtes pas revenus à moi, déclare le SEIGNEUR" (B); "Mais même alors, vous n'êtes pas revenus vers moi, dit le SEIGNEUR" (R)
alternatives: "vous ne vous êtes pas tournés vers moi"
decisions.reason: One wording at each level for all five verses, with "revenir", the French prophets' verb for shuv at every level.

decisions.choice: "lakini hamkurudi kwangu, asema BWANA" (L); "Hata hivyo hamkurudi kwangu, asema BWANA" (B); "Lakini hata hivyo hamkurudi kwangu, anasema BWANA" (R)
decisions.reason: The refrain of 4:6-11 keeps one wording at each level; "kurudi" is the word for turning back to God in Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: "thế mà các ngươi vẫn không quay về với Ta, CHÚA phán vậy" (L, B); "Dù vậy, các ngươi vẫn không ăn năn quay về với Ta, CHÚA phán" (R)
alternatives: "Các ngươi cũng chẳng trở lại cùng ta"
decisions.reason: The refrain of 4:6-11 keeps one wording at each level. Turning back in repentance is "quay về" (L, B) and "ăn năn quay về" (R), as the Jeremiah note settles for shuv.

decisions.choice: The refrain of 4:6–11: "그러나 너희는 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다." (L); "그래도 너희는 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다." (B); "그래도 너희는 여전히 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다." (R)
decisions.reason: One wording per level in all five verses; *shuv* is "돌아오다", as in Joel 2:12.

decisions.choice: "răng sạch trơn" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the image of teeth with nothing to chew, as the English "clean teeth"; Readable says plainly that they went hungry.

decisions.choice: "이를 깨끗하게 하고" (L, B); "굶주리게 했다" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew picture, nothing left to chew, which the meaning decision explains; Readable says the famine.

source.text: וְגַ֣ם אָנֹכִי֩ מָנַ֨עְתִּי מִכֶּ֜ם אֶת־הַגֶּ֗שֶׁם בְּע֨וֹד שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ לַקָּצִ֔יר וְהִמְטַרְתִּי֙ עַל־עִ֣יר אֶחָ֔ת וְעַל־עִ֥יר אַחַ֖ת לֹ֣א אַמְטִ֑יר חֶלְקָ֤ה אַחַת֙ תִּמָּטֵ֔ר וְחֶלְקָ֛ה אֲשֶֽׁר־לֹֽא־תַמְטִ֥יר עָלֶ֖יהָ תִּיבָֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And also I withheld from you the rain while yet three months to the harvest; and I would send rain on one city, and on another city I would not send rain; one portion would be rained on, and [the] portion on which it did not rain would wither.

en.L: And I also withheld the rain from you while [it was] still three months to the harvest; \q and I would send rain on one city, \q and on another city I would not send rain; \q one field would be rained on, \q and the field on which it did not rain would wither.
en.B: I also held back the rain from you when the harvest was still three months away. \q I would send rain on one town \q but no rain on another. \q One field would get rain, \q and the field that got none would dry up.
en.R: I also kept the rain from you when the harvest was still three months away. \q I sent rain on one town \q but not on another. \q One field got rain, \q but a field without rain dried up.

es.L: Y también yo {{plural_you:les|os}} retuve la lluvia cuando aún faltaban tres meses para la siega; \q e hice llover sobre una ciudad, \q y sobre otra ciudad no hice llover; \q sobre un campo llovía, \q y el campo sobre el cual no llovía se secaba.
es.B: También {{plural_you:les|os}} retuve la lluvia cuando todavía faltaban tres meses para la cosecha. \q Hacía llover sobre un pueblo \q y sobre otro no. \q Un campo recibía lluvia, \q y el que no la recibía se secaba.
es.R: También {{plural_you:les|os}} quité la lluvia cuando todavía faltaban tres meses para la cosecha. \q Envié lluvia sobre un pueblo \q pero no sobre otro. \q Un campo recibió lluvia, \q pero el campo que no la recibió se secó.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi, je vous ai refusé la pluie quand [il y avait] encore trois mois jusqu’à la moisson ; \q et je faisais pleuvoir sur une ville, \q et sur une autre ville je ne faisais pas pleuvoir ; \q un champ recevait la pluie, \q et le champ sur lequel il ne pleuvait pas se desséchait.
fr.B: Je vous ai aussi privés de pluie quand la moisson était encore à trois mois. \q Je faisais pleuvoir sur une ville \q mais pas sur une autre. \q Un champ recevait la pluie, \q et le champ qui n’en recevait pas se desséchait.
fr.R: Je vous ai aussi privés de pluie quand la moisson était encore à trois mois. \q J’envoyais la pluie sur une ville \q mais pas sur une autre. \q Un champ recevait la pluie, \q mais un champ sans pluie se desséchait.

sw.L: Nami pia niliwazuilia mvua [ilipokuwa] bado miezi mitatu kabla ya mavuno; \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} ningenyesha mvua juu ya mji mmoja, \q na juu ya mji mwingine nisinyeshe mvua; \q shamba moja lingenyeshewa mvua, \q na shamba lisilonyeshewa mvua lingenyauka.
sw.B: Pia niliwazuilia mvua wakati mavuno yalipokuwa bado miezi mitatu. \q Ningenyesha mvua juu ya mji mmoja \q lakini nisinyeshe juu ya mji mwingine. \q Shamba moja lingepata mvua, \q na shamba lisilopata mvua lingekauka.
sw.R: Pia niliizuia mvua isiwanyeshee wakati mavuno yalipokuwa bado miezi mitatu. \q Nilinyesha mvua juu ya mji mmoja \q lakini sikunyesha juu ya mwingine. \q Shamba moja lilipata mvua, \q lakini shamba lisilopata mvua likakauka.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng đã cầm giữ mưa khỏi các ngươi khi còn ba tháng nữa mới đến mùa gặt; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho mưa xuống trên thành này, \q còn trên thành khác {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không cho mưa; \q ruộng này được mưa, \q còn ruộng không có mưa thì khô héo.
vi.B: Ta cũng đã giữ mưa lại không cho các ngươi khi còn ba tháng nữa mới đến mùa gặt. \q Ta cho mưa xuống trên thị trấn này \q nhưng không cho mưa trên thị trấn kia. \q Ruộng này có mưa, \q còn ruộng không có mưa thì khô cằn.
vi.R: Ta cũng đã không cho mưa khi còn ba tháng nữa mới đến mùa gặt. \q Ta cho mưa xuống trên thị trấn này \q nhưng không cho mưa trên thị trấn kia. \q Ruộng này có mưa, \q còn ruộng không có mưa thì khô cằn.

ko.L: 그리고 추수하기까지 아직 석 달이 남았을 때에 내가 너희에게서 비를 거두었다. \q 내가 한 성읍에는 비를 내리고 \q 다른 성읍에는 비를 내리지 않았다. \q 한 밭은 비를 맞고, \q 비를 맞지 못한 밭은 말라 버렸다.
ko.B: 추수가 아직 석 달이나 남았을 때에 나는 너희에게 비를 내리지 않았다. \q 한 마을에는 비를 내리고 \q 다른 마을에는 내리지 않았다. \q 한 밭에는 비가 왔고, \q 비가 오지 않은 밭은 말라 버렸다.
ko.R: 추수가 아직 석 달이나 남았을 때에 나는 비를 멈추었다. \q 한 마을에는 비를 내렸지만 \q 다른 마을에는 내리지 않았다. \q 어떤 밭에는 비가 왔지만, \q 비가 오지 않은 밭은 말라 버렸다.

decisions.choice: the rain withheld three months before the harvest: the late rains that the grain needed
decisions.reason: In Israel the rains fall from autumn to spring. The last rains, in late winter and spring, swell the grain before the harvest in April and May (Deuteronomy 11:14; Jeremiah 3:3; Joel 2:23). Without them the crop fails.

decisions.choice: rain on one town and not on another: a sign that the drought came from the LORD
decisions.reason: Rain falling on one town and not the next, on one field and not its neighbor, showed that this was no ordinary dry season. The covenant tied the rain to Israel's faithfulness (Deuteronomy 11:13-17; 1 Kings 8:35-36; 17:1). The verbs describe something that happened again and again.

decisions.choice: city (L), town (B, R); portion of ground (L field), field (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word for "city" is used of any walled town, and "town" fits the many small places meant here. The word translated "field" means a portion of land, a plot.

decisions.choice: imparfait "je faisais pleuvoir", "recevait", "se desséchait"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes what happened again and again during the drought; French uses the imparfait for repeated action.

source.text: וְנָע֡וּ שְׁתַּיִם֩ שָׁלֹ֨שׁ עָרִ֜ים אֶל־עִ֥יר אַחַ֛ת לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת מַ֖יִם וְלֹ֣א יִשְׂבָּ֑עוּ וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And staggered two, three cities to one city to drink water, and not they were satisfied; yet not you returned to me, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And two, three cities staggered to one city to drink water, and they were not filled; \q yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: People from two or three towns staggered to another town for water but could not get enough to drink. \q Yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: People from two or three towns stumbled to another town for water, but there was not enough to drink. \q But even then you did not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y dos, tres ciudades iban tambaleándose a una ciudad para beber agua, y no se saciaban; \q y no {{plural_you:volvieron|volvisteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: La gente de dos o tres pueblos iba tambaleándose a otro pueblo en busca de agua, pero no lograba beber lo suficiente. \q Pero no {{plural_you:volvieron|volvisteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: La gente de dos o tres pueblos iba a otro pueblo tropezando en busca de agua, pero no había suficiente para beber. \q Pero aun así no {{plural_you:regresaron|regresasteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et deux, trois villes allaient en titubant vers une ville pour boire de l’eau, et elles n’étaient pas rassasiées ; \q et vous n’êtes pas revenus à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Les gens de deux ou trois villes allaient en titubant vers une autre ville pour trouver de l’eau, mais ne pouvaient pas boire à leur soif. \q Pourtant, vous n’êtes pas revenus à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Les gens de deux ou trois villes se traînaient jusqu’à une autre ville pour trouver de l’eau, mais il n’y en avait pas assez pour boire. \q Mais même alors, vous n’êtes pas revenus vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Na miji miwili, mitatu ikayumbayumba kwenda mji mmoja kunywa maji, wala hawakushiba; \q lakini hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Watu wa miji miwili au mitatu walijikokota hadi mji mwingine kutafuta maji, lakini hawakupata ya kutosha kunywa. \q Hata hivyo hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Watu wa miji miwili au mitatu walijikokota hadi mji mwingine kutafuta maji, lakini hapakuwa na ya kutosha kunywa. \q Lakini hata hivyo hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Và hai, ba thành lảo đảo đến một thành để uống nước, mà không được thỏa; \q thế mà các ngươi vẫn không quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Dân hai ba thị trấn lảo đảo đến một thị trấn khác tìm nước, nhưng không có đủ để uống. \q Thế mà các ngươi vẫn không quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Dân hai ba thị trấn lê bước đến một thị trấn khác để tìm nước, nhưng không có đủ nước uống. \q Dù vậy, các ngươi vẫn không ăn năn quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 두세 성읍이 물을 마시려고 한 성읍으로 비틀거리며 갔으나 배를 채우지 못했다. \q 그러나 너희는 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 두세 마을 사람들이 물을 마시려고 다른 마을로 비틀거리며 갔으나, 실컷 마시지 못했다. \q 그래도 너희는 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 두세 마을 사람들이 물을 찾아 다른 마을로 비틀비틀 걸어갔지만, 마실 물이 넉넉하지 않았다. \q 그래도 너희는 여전히 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: two, three cities: several towns
decisions.reason: "Two, three" means a few, several (compare Isaiah 17:6). The people of several towns went, weak with thirst, to one town that still had water.

decisions.choice: staggered: went unsteadily, weak from thirst
decisions.reason: The verb means to wander or to stagger (Psalm 107:27; Lamentations 4:14-15).

decisions.choice: yet you did not return to me: the refrain of 4:6-11, as in 4:6
decisions.reason: The same words close each of the LORD's blows in verses 6-11. On their meaning, see the note at 4:6.

decisions.choice: People from (B, R); towns (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that the towns staggered; Balanced and Readable say that their people did.

source.text: הִכֵּ֣יתִי אֶתְכֶם֮ בַּשִּׁדָּפ֣וֹן וּבַיֵּרָקוֹן֒ הַרְבּ֨וֹת גַּנּוֹתֵיכֶ֧ם וְכַרְמֵיכֶ֛ם וּתְאֵנֵיכֶ֥ם וְזֵיתֵיכֶ֖ם יֹאכַ֣ל הַגָּזָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: I struck you with blight and with mildew; [the] many of your gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees, the locust devoured; yet not you returned to me, declares Yahweh.

en.L: I struck you with blight and with mildew; \q the many of your gardens and your vineyards, your fig trees and your olive trees, the cutting locust devoured; \q yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I struck you with blight and mildew; \q the cutting locust devoured your many gardens and vineyards, your fig trees and olive groves. \q Yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I struck your crops with diseases that dried them out and turned them yellow. \q Locusts ate up your many gardens and vineyards, and your fig trees and olive trees. \q But even then you did not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} herí con tizón y con añublo; \q la multitud de {{plural_you:sus huertos|vuestros huertos}} y {{plural_you:sus viñas|vuestras viñas}}, {{plural_you:sus higueras|vuestras higueras}} y {{plural_you:sus olivos|vuestros olivos}}, la devoró la langosta cortadora; \q y no {{plural_you:volvieron|volvisteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} herí con tizón y con añublo; \q la langosta cortadora devoró {{plural_you:sus muchos huertos y viñas|vuestros muchos huertos y viñas}}, {{plural_you:sus higueras y olivares|vuestras higueras y olivares}}. \q Pero no {{plural_you:volvieron|volvisteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Mandé sobre {{plural_you:sus cosechas|vuestras cosechas}} plagas que las secaban y las ponían amarillas. \q Las langostas se comieron {{plural_you:sus muchos huertos y viñas|vuestros muchos huertos y viñas}}, y {{plural_you:sus higueras y olivos|vuestras higueras y olivos}}. \q Pero aun así no {{plural_you:regresaron|regresasteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Je vous ai frappés par la rouille et par la nielle ; \q la multitude de vos jardins et de vos vignes, de vos figuiers et de vos oliviers, la sauterelle qui ronge [l’]a dévorée ; \q et vous n’êtes pas revenus à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Je vous ai frappés par la rouille et la nielle ; \q la sauterelle qui ronge a dévoré vos nombreux jardins et vos vignes, vos figuiers et vos oliviers. \q Pourtant, vous n’êtes pas revenus à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: J’ai frappé vos récoltes de maladies qui les ont desséchées et jaunies. \q Les sauterelles ont dévoré vos nombreux jardins et vos vignes, vos figuiers et vos oliviers. \q Mais même alors, vous n’êtes pas revenus vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Niliwapiga kwa ukaukaji na kwa ukungu; \q wingi wa bustani zenu na mashamba yenu ya mizabibu, mitini yenu na mizeituni yenu, nzige wakataji waliila; \q lakini hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Niliwapiga kwa ukaukaji na ukungu; \q nzige wakataji walizila bustani zenu nyingi na mashamba ya mizabibu, mitini yenu na mizeituni yenu. \q Hata hivyo hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Nilipiga mazao yenu kwa magonjwa yaliyoyakausha na kuyageuza manjano. \q Nzige walikula bustani zenu nyingi na mashamba ya mizabibu, mitini na mizeituni yenu. \q Lakini hata hivyo hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Ta đã đánh các ngươi bằng bệnh lúa héo và nấm mốc; \q biết bao vườn tược và vườn nho, cây vả và cây ô-liu của các ngươi, châu chấu cắn phá đã ăn nuốt; \q thế mà các ngươi vẫn không quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Ta đã đánh các ngươi bằng bệnh lúa héo và nấm mốc; \q châu chấu cắn phá đã ăn nuốt biết bao vườn tược và vườn nho, cây vả và vườn ô-liu của các ngươi. \q Thế mà các ngươi vẫn không quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Ta đã giáng trên mùa màng các ngươi những bệnh làm cho cây khô héo và vàng úa. \q Châu chấu đã ăn sạch biết bao vườn tược, vườn nho, cây vả và cây ô-liu của các ngươi. \q Dù vậy, các ngươi vẫn không ăn năn quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 내가 마름병과 깜부기병으로 너희를 쳤다. \q 너희의 많은 동산과 포도원, 너희의 무화과나무와 올리브나무를 자르는 메뚜기가 먹어 치웠다. \q 그러나 너희는 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 내가 마름병과 깜부기병으로 너희를 쳤다. \q 자르는 메뚜기가 너희의 많은 동산과 포도원, 무화과나무와 올리브나무를 먹어 치웠다. \q 그래도 너희는 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 나는 너희의 곡식을 병들게 하여, 말라 버리고 누렇게 변하게 했다. \q 메뚜기 떼가 너희의 많은 밭과 포도원, 무화과나무와 올리브나무를 먹어 치웠다. \q 그래도 너희는 여전히 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: blight and mildew: grain scorched by the hot wind and yellowed by disease
decisions.reason: The first word means scorching, the withering of grain by the hot east wind (Genesis 41:6); the second means a yellowing, mildew or rust. The two are named together among the covenant curses (Deuteronomy 28:22) and in Solomon's prayer (1 Kings 8:37).

decisions.choice: Haggai 2:17 repeats these words
decisions.reason: Haggai 2:17 takes up this verse: "I struck you with blight and mildew and hail ... yet you did not turn to me, declares the LORD". Haggai applies Amos's words to the people of his own day.

decisions.choice: the many of your gardens: your many gardens
alternatives: I laid waste your gardens and vineyards
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is a verb form meaning "making many", used here as "your many gardens". It is awkward, and a small change of letters would give "I laid waste your gardens", which some prefer.

decisions.choice: the cutting locust: one of the names for the locust
decisions.reason: The word is the first of the four names for locusts in Joel 1:4, where they may be kinds or stages of the insect. Here it stands for a swarm that ate everything.

decisions.choice: yet you did not return to me: the refrain of 4:6-11, as in 4:6
decisions.reason: The same words close each of the LORD's blows in verses 6-11. On their meaning, see the note at 4:6.

decisions.choice: blight and mildew (L, B), diseases that dried them out and turned them yellow (R); the cutting locust (L, B), Locusts (R)
decisions.reason: "The cutting locust" is the wording used for this word in Joel 1:4; Readable says "locusts", as Readable does there. Readable explains the two crop diseases (m1).

decisions.choice: "tizón y añublo" (L, B); "la langosta cortadora" (L, B), "Las langostas" (R)
decisions.reason: The two crop diseases by their Spanish farming names; gazam is "la langosta cortadora", as set for Joel 1:4 and 2:25.

decisions.choice: "la rouille et la nielle" (L, B); "la sauterelle qui ronge" (L, B)
decisions.reason: French farmers' names for grain scorched and yellowed by disease; the locust is the one Joel's French calls "la sauterelle qui ronge".

decisions.choice: "nzige wakataji" (L, B); "Nzige" (R)
decisions.reason: Gazam, the cutting locust, as the locust names in Joel.

decisions.choice: "châu chấu cắn phá" (L, B); "châu chấu" (R)
decisions.reason: Gazam is the locust name of Joel 1:4 and 2:25, "châu chấu cắn phá" in the terms sheet; Readable says simply "châu chấu".

decisions.choice: "마름병과 곰팡이병" (L, B), as Haggai 2:17; "자르는 메뚜기" (L, B), Joel's word for gazam
decisions.reason: Haggai 2:17 quotes this verse, so the two diseases and the refrain share Haggai's wording at each level; the locust takes the term sheet's Joel wording.

source.text: שִׁלַּ֨חְתִּי בָכֶ֥ם דֶּ֨בֶר֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם הָרַ֤גְתִּי בַחֶ֨רֶב֙ בַּח֣וּרֵיכֶ֔ם עִ֖ם שְׁבִ֣י סֽוּסֵיכֶ֑ם וָאַעֲלֶ֞ה בְּאֹ֤שׁ מַחֲנֵיכֶם֙ וּֽבְאַפְּכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: I sent among you pestilence after [the] manner of Egypt; I killed with the sword your young men, along with [the] capture of your horses, and I made go up [the] stench of your camps even into your nostrils; yet not you returned to me, declares Yahweh.

en.L: I sent pestilence among you in the manner of Egypt; \q I killed with the sword your young men, \q along with your captured horses; \q and I made the stench of your camps rise even into your nostrils; \q yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I sent a plague among you as I did on Egypt; \q I killed your young men with the sword, \q and your horses were captured; \q I made the stench of your camps fill your nostrils. \q Yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I sent diseases among you like the ones I sent on Egypt. \q I killed your young men in battle, \q and your horses were taken away. \q I made you smell the stink of dead bodies in your camps. \q But even then you did not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Envié entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} peste a la manera de Egipto; \q maté a espada a {{plural_you:sus jóvenes|vuestros jóvenes}}, \q junto con {{plural_you:sus caballos|vuestros caballos}} capturados; \q e hice subir el hedor de {{plural_you:sus campamentos|vuestros campamentos}} hasta {{plural_you:sus narices|vuestras narices}}; \q y no {{plural_you:volvieron|volvisteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Envié una plaga entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} como hice con Egipto; \q maté a espada a {{plural_you:sus jóvenes|vuestros jóvenes}}, \q y {{plural_you:sus caballos|vuestros caballos}} fueron capturados; \q hice que el hedor de {{plural_you:sus campamentos|vuestros campamentos}} {{plural_you:les llenara la nariz|os llenara la nariz}}. \q Pero no {{plural_you:volvieron|volvisteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Envié enfermedades entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} como las que envié sobre Egipto. \q Maté a {{plural_you:sus jóvenes|vuestros jóvenes}} en la batalla, \q y se llevaron {{plural_you:sus caballos|vuestros caballos}}. \q Hice que {{plural_you:olieran|olierais}} la peste de los cadáveres en {{plural_you:sus campamentos|vuestros campamentos}}. \q Pero aun así no {{plural_you:regresaron|regresasteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: J’ai envoyé la peste parmi vous à la manière de l’Égypte ; \q j’ai tué par l’épée vos jeunes hommes, \q avec vos chevaux capturés ; \q et j’ai fait monter la puanteur de vos camps jusque dans vos narines ; \q et vous n’êtes pas revenus à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: J’ai envoyé la peste parmi vous, comme je l’ai fait sur l’Égypte ; \q j’ai tué vos jeunes hommes par l’épée, \q et vos chevaux ont été capturés ; \q j’ai fait monter jusqu’à vos narines la puanteur de vos camps. \q Pourtant, vous n’êtes pas revenus à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Je vous ai envoyé des maladies comme celles que j’ai envoyées sur l’Égypte. \q J’ai tué vos jeunes hommes à la guerre, \q et vos chevaux ont été emmenés. \q Je vous ai fait sentir l’odeur des cadavres dans vos camps. \q Mais même alors, vous n’êtes pas revenus vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nilituma tauni kati yenu kwa namna ya Misri; \q niliwaua vijana wenu kwa upanga, \q pamoja na farasi wenu waliotekwa; \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nikapandisha uvundo wa kambi zenu hata ndani ya pua zenu; \q lakini hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Nilituma tauni kati yenu kama nilivyofanya kwa Misri; \q niliwaua vijana wenu kwa upanga, \q na farasi wenu wakatekwa; \q niliufanya uvundo wa kambi zenu ujaze pua zenu. \q Hata hivyo hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Niliwaletea magonjwa kama yale niliyoyaleta juu ya Misri. \q Niliwaua vijana wenu vitani, \q na farasi wenu wakachukuliwa. \q Niliwafanya mnuse harufu mbaya ya maiti katika kambi zenu. \q Lakini hata hivyo hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Ta đã sai dịch lệ đến giữa các ngươi như cách [{{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã làm cho] Ai Cập; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã dùng gươm giết các thanh niên của các ngươi, \q cùng với những ngựa bị bắt của các ngươi; \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã làm cho mùi hôi thối của các trại quân các ngươi xông lên tận mũi các ngươi; \q thế mà các ngươi vẫn không quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Ta đã sai dịch bệnh đến giữa các ngươi như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã làm cho Ai Cập; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã dùng gươm giết các thanh niên của các ngươi, \q và ngựa của các ngươi bị bắt mất; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã làm cho mùi hôi thối của các trại quân xộc vào mũi các ngươi. \q Thế mà các ngươi vẫn không quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Ta đã sai bệnh tật đến giữa các ngươi, giống như những bệnh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã sai đến trên Ai Cập. \q Ta đã giết các thanh niên của các ngươi trong chiến trận, \q và ngựa của các ngươi bị cướp đi. \q Ta đã làm cho các ngươi phải ngửi mùi hôi thối của xác chết trong các trại quân. \q Dù vậy, các ngươi vẫn không ăn năn quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 내가 이집트에서 [한] 방식대로 너희 가운데 전염병을 보냈다. \q 내가 너희 젊은이들을 칼로 죽이고, \q 너희 말들을 빼앗기게 했다. \q 너희 진영의 악취가 너희 코에까지 올라오게 했다. \q 그러나 너희는 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 내가 이집트에 한 것처럼 너희 가운데 전염병을 보냈다. \q 너희 젊은이들을 칼로 죽였고, \q 너희 말들은 빼앗겼다. \q 너희 진영의 악취가 너희 코를 찌르게 했다. \q 그래도 너희는 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 나는 이집트에 보냈던 것과 같은 질병을 너희 가운데 보냈다. \q 너희 젊은이들을 전쟁에서 죽게 했고, \q 너희 말들은 적에게 빼앗겼다. \q 너희 진영에서 시체 썩는 냄새가 나게 했다. \q 그래도 너희는 여전히 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: pestilence in the manner of Egypt: the plagues the LORD once sent on Egypt now strike Israel
decisions.reason: The LORD struck Egypt with pestilence (Exodus 9:3, 15), and the covenant warned that Israel would suffer "the diseases of Egypt" if it turned away (Deuteronomy 28:27, 60). "In the manner of" may also be read "on the road to" Egypt, but the link with the exodus plagues fits the verse best.

decisions.choice: young men killed, horses captured: defeat in war
decisions.reason: Israel's young men died in battle and its horses, the strength of its chariot force, were taken. In the wars with Aram Israel was left with only fifty horsemen and ten chariots (2 Kings 13:7).

decisions.choice: the stench of your camps: the smell of the unburied dead
decisions.reason: After defeat, the dead lay unburied in the army's camp, and the stench rose (Isaiah 34:3; Joel 2:20).

decisions.choice: yet you did not return to me: the refrain of 4:6-11, as in 4:6
decisions.reason: The same words close each of the LORD's blows in verses 6-11. On their meaning, see the note at 4:6.

decisions.choice: pestilence (L), plague (B), diseases (R); in battle (R); dead bodies (R)
decisions.reason: "Pestilence", "plague" and "disease" are the settled wording for this word. Readable says "in battle" for "with the sword" and says what made the stench (m3).

source.text: הָפַ֣כְתִּי בָכֶ֗ם כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֤ת אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־סְדֹ֣ם וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָ֔ה וַתִּהְי֕וּ כְּא֖וּד מֻצָּ֣ל מִשְׂרֵפָ֑הוְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: I overthrew among you as [the] overthrow of God [of] Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a firebrand snatched from [the] burning; yet not you returned to me, declares Yahweh.

en.L: I overthrew [some] among you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, \q and you were like a stick snatched from the burning; \q yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I overthrew some of you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, \q and you became like a burning stick pulled out of the fire. \q Yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I destroyed some of you as completely as God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. \q The rest of you were like a burning stick pulled out of a fire just in time. \q But even then you did not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Trastorné [a algunos] entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, como Dios trastornó a Sodoma y a Gomorra, \q y {{plural_you:fueron|fuisteis}} como un tizón arrancado del fuego; \q y no {{plural_you:volvieron|volvisteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Destruí a algunos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} como Dios destruyó a Sodoma y Gomorra, \q y {{plural_you:quedaron|quedasteis}} como un palo encendido sacado del fuego. \q Pero no {{plural_you:volvieron|volvisteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Destruí a algunos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tan completamente como Dios destruyó a Sodoma y Gomorra. \q Los demás {{plural_you:quedaron|quedasteis}} como un palo encendido que se saca del fuego justo a tiempo. \q Pero aun así no {{plural_you:regresaron|regresasteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: J’ai bouleversé [certains] parmi vous, comme Dieu a bouleversé Sodome et Gomorrhe, \q et vous avez été comme un tison arraché de l’incendie ; \q et vous n’êtes pas revenus à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: J’ai bouleversé certains d’entre vous comme Dieu a bouleversé Sodome et Gomorrhe, \q et vous êtes devenus comme un tison retiré du feu. \q Pourtant, vous n’êtes pas revenus à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: J’ai détruit certains d’entre vous aussi complètement que Dieu a détruit Sodome et Gomorrhe. \q Les autres étaient comme un bâton en flammes qu’on retire du feu juste à temps. \q Mais même alors, vous n’êtes pas revenus vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Niliwaangamiza [baadhi] kati yenu, kama Mungu alivyoziangamiza Sodoma na Gomora, \q nanyi mlikuwa kama kijinga kilichonyakuliwa motoni; \q lakini hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Niliwaangamiza baadhi yenu kama Mungu alivyoziangamiza Sodoma na Gomora, \q nanyi mkawa kama kijinga kinachowaka kilichotolewa motoni. \q Hata hivyo hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Niliwaangamiza baadhi yenu kabisa, kama Mungu alivyoziangamiza Sodoma na Gomora. \q Wengine wenu mlikuwa kama kijinga kinachowaka kilichotolewa motoni dakika ya mwisho. \q Lakini hata hivyo hamkurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Ta đã lật đổ [một số] trong các ngươi, như Đức Chúa Trời đã lật đổ Sô-đôm và Gô-mô-rơ, \q và các ngươi như que củi được rút ra khỏi đám cháy; \q thế mà các ngươi vẫn không quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Ta đã lật đổ một số người trong các ngươi như Đức Chúa Trời đã lật đổ Sô-đôm và Gô-mô-rơ, \q và các ngươi như que củi đang cháy được kéo ra khỏi lửa. \q Thế mà các ngươi vẫn không quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Ta đã hủy diệt một số người trong các ngươi hoàn toàn như Đức Chúa Trời đã hủy diệt Sô-đôm và Gô-mô-rơ. \q Số còn lại như que củi đang cháy được kéo ra khỏi lửa vừa kịp lúc. \q Dù vậy, các ngươi vẫn không ăn năn quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 하나님께서 소돔과 고모라를 뒤엎으신 것처럼 \q 내가 너희 가운데 [몇을] 뒤엎었다. 너희는 불 속에서 건져 낸 나무토막 같았다. \q 그러나 너희는 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 소돔과 고모라를 뒤엎으신 것처럼 \q 내가 너희 가운데 몇을 뒤엎었다. 너희는 불 속에서 끄집어낸 타다 남은 나무토막처럼 되었다. \q 그래도 너희는 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 소돔과 고모라를 완전히 멸망시키신 것처럼 \q 나는 너희 가운데 몇을 멸망시켰다. 나머지는 불 속에서 겨우 끄집어낸 타다 남은 나무토막 같았다. \q 그래도 너희는 여전히 나에게 돌아오지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah: utter destruction
decisions.reason: The overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:24-25) became the standard picture of total ruin (Deuteronomy 29:22; Isaiah 1:9; 13:19; Jeremiah 49:18). The LORD speaks of himself as "God" because the phrase is a fixed one (Isaiah 13:19; Jeremiah 50:40). The text does not say what disaster struck part of Israel in this way; it may have been war, or an earthquake like the one in 1:1.

decisions.choice: a stick snatched from the burning: barely saved, already scorched
decisions.reason: A stick pulled out of the fire is saved, but only just, and it is charred (Zechariah 3:2). Israel had survived, but narrowly, and still it did not return.

decisions.choice: yet you did not return to me: the refrain of 4:6-11, as in 4:6
decisions.reason: The same words close each of the LORD's blows in verses 6-11. On their meaning, see the note at 4:6.

decisions.choice: some (L in brackets, B, R); as completely as; the rest of you; just in time (R)
decisions.reason: "Among you" means that part of the people was struck, and every level supplies "some". Readable says what the comparisons mean (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: "하나님이 소돔과 고모라를 뒤엎은 것처럼", without -시-
decisions.reason: God himself is speaking, so the third-person "God" in his mouth takes no honorific, as God never takes -시- in his own words.

source.text: לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂה־לְּךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עֵ֚קֶב כִּֽי־זֹ֣את אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּ֔ךְ הִכּ֥וֹן לִקְרַאת־אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus I will do to you, Israel; because this I will do to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel.

en.L: Therefore thus I will do to you, O Israel; \q because this I will do to you, \q prepare to meet your God, O Israel!
en.B: So this is what I will do to you, Israel; \q and because I am going to do this to you, \q prepare to meet your God, Israel!
en.R: So, Israel, this is what I will do to you. \q And because I am going to do this to you, \q get ready to meet your God, Israel!

es.L: Por tanto, así te haré a ti, oh Israel; \q y porque esto te haré, \q ¡prepárate para encontrarte con tu Dios, oh Israel!
es.B: Por eso, esto es lo que te haré, Israel; \q y porque voy a hacerte esto, \q ¡prepárate para encontrarte con tu Dios, Israel!
es.R: Por eso, Israel, esto es lo que te haré. \q Y porque voy a hacerte esto, \q ¡prepárate para encontrarte con tu Dios, Israel!

fr.L: C’est pourquoi je te ferai ainsi, ô Israël ; \q parce que je te ferai cela, \q prépare-toi à rencontrer ton Dieu, ô Israël !
fr.B: Voilà donc ce que je vais te faire, Israël ; \q et puisque je vais te faire cela, \q prépare-toi à rencontrer ton Dieu, Israël !
fr.R: Israël, voilà ce que je vais te faire. \q Et puisque je vais te faire cela, \q prépare-toi à rencontrer ton Dieu, Israël !

sw.L: Kwa hiyo hivi ndivyo nitakavyokutendea, ee Israeli; \q kwa sababu nitakutendea hili, \q jiandae kukutana na Mungu wako, ee Israeli!
sw.B: Basi hivi ndivyo nitakavyokutendea, Israeli; \q na kwa kuwa nitakutendea hili, \q jiandae kukutana na Mungu wako, Israeli!
sw.R: Basi, Israeli, hivi ndivyo nitakavyokutendea. \q Na kwa kuwa nitakutendea hili, \q jiweke tayari kukutana na Mungu wako, Israeli!

vi.L: Vì vậy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho ngươi như thế, hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên; \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm điều này cho ngươi, \q hãy sửa soạn để gặp Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên!
vi.B: Vậy đây là điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho ngươi, hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên; \q và vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sắp làm điều này cho ngươi, \q hãy chuẩn bị để gặp Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên!
vi.R: Vậy, hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, đây là điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho ngươi. \q Và vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sắp làm điều này cho ngươi, \q hãy sẵn sàng gặp Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên!

ko.L: 그러므로 이스라엘아, 내가 너에게 이렇게 하겠다. \q 내가 너에게 이것을 할 것이니, \q 이스라엘아, 네 하나님을 만날 준비를 하여라!
ko.B: 그러므로 이스라엘아, 내가 너에게 이렇게 하겠다. \q 내가 너에게 이 일을 하려고 하니, \q 이스라엘아, 네 하나님을 만날 준비를 하여라!
ko.R: 그러니 이스라엘아, 나는 너에게 이렇게 하겠다. \q 내가 너에게 이 일을 하려고 하니, \q 이스라엘아, 네 하나님을 만날 준비를 하여라!

decisions.choice: thus I will do to you: what the LORD will do is not said
decisions.reason: "Thus" and "this" usually point to something said next, but nothing follows. The LORD leaves the threat open, which makes it more fearful than any description. Some take "this" to point back to the judgments already announced (3:11-15; 4:2-3), others forward to the meeting with God in the same verse.

decisions.choice: prepare to meet your God: the words of Sinai, now a summons to judgment
decisions.reason: At Sinai the people were told to "be ready", and Moses brought them out "to meet God" (Exodus 19:11, 15, 17). Israel will meet its God again, but after five refusals to return (verses 6-11) the meeting will be for judgment. Some hear in the words a last call to repent before that meeting, but the verse itself announces it.

decisions.choice: O Israel (L), Israel (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal marks the calling out of Israel's name with "O", as in Hosea; Balanced and Readable use the name alone. Readable says "get ready" for "prepare".

decisions.choice: tú to Israel
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew speaks to Israel in the singular, as one person, so Spanish uses tú and no plural_you span.

decisions.choice: "te", "ton": Israël in the singular
decisions.reason: After the plural of verses 4-11, the Hebrew speaks to Israel as one person, and French follows its number.

decisions.choice: "ngươi" for Israel addressed as one
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns from the plural "you" of verses 6-11 to the singular, Israel as one person summoned before God; "ngươi" keeps that, as the rebuke address of the terms sheet.

source.text: כִּ֡י הִנֵּה֩ יוֹצֵ֨ר הָרִ֜ים וּבֹרֵ֣א ר֗וּחַ וּמַגִּ֤יד לְאָדָם֙ מַה־שֵּׂח֔וֹ עֹשֵׂ֥ה שַׁ֨חַר֙ עֵיפָ֔ה וְדֹרֵ֖ךְ עַל־בָּ֣מֳתֵי אָ֑רֶץ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For look, [the one] forming mountains and creating wind, and declaring to humankind what [is] his thought, making dawn darkness, and treading on [the] heights of [the] earth: Yahweh, God of hosts, [is] his name.

en.L: For look, the one who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to humankind what {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} thought [is], \q who makes the dawn darkness, \q and treads on the earth's heights: \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who forms the mountains and creates the wind, who reveals {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} thoughts to humankind, \q who turns the dawn into darkness \q and treads on the heights of the earth: \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.R: He formed the mountains and created the wind. He tells people what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is planning. \q He turns the dawn into darkness \q and walks on the high places of the earth. \q His name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies.

es.L: Porque he aquí, el que forma los montes y crea el viento, y declara al ser humano cuál [es] {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pensamiento, \q el que hace de la aurora tinieblas, \q y camina sobre las alturas de la tierra: \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los ejércitos [es] {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.B: Porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es quien forma los montes y crea el viento, quien revela a la humanidad {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pensamientos, \q quien convierte la aurora en tinieblas \q y camina sobre las alturas de la tierra: \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.R: Él formó los montes y creó el viento. Él les dice a los seres humanos lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} piensa hacer. \q Él convierte el amanecer en oscuridad \q y camina sobre los lugares altos de la tierra. \q Su nombre es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos.

fr.L: Car voici, celui qui forme les montagnes et crée le vent, et qui révèle {{gender:à l’être humain|à l’homme}} quelle [est] {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} pensée, \q qui fait de l’aurore les ténèbres, \q et marche sur les hauteurs de la terre : \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, [est] {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.
fr.B: Car c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui forme les montagnes et crée le vent, qui fait connaître {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pensées {{gender:aux humains|aux hommes}}, \q qui change l’aurore en ténèbres \q et marche sur les hauteurs de la terre : \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, est {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.
fr.R: Il a formé les montagnes et créé le vent. Il dit aux gens ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a l’intention de faire. \q Il change l’aurore en ténèbres \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} marche sur les hauteurs de la terre. \q Son nom est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées.
